questions.question: What does $X_n\xrightarrow{d}X$ require of the CDFs $F_{X_n}$ and $F_X$?
options: $F_{X_n}(x)\to F_X(x)$ at every $x$ where $F_X$ is continuous
The densities satisfy $f_{X_n}(x)\to f_X(x)$ at every $x$

questions.question: What does the statement $X_n\xrightarrow{d}\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ assert, with $\Phi$ the standard normal CDF?
options: $X_n$ equals a normal variable once $n$ is large
The means and variances of $X_n$ tend to $0$ and $1$

questions.question: Let $X_n=2+1/n$ and let $X=2$ be constant. Which pair $(F_{X_n}(2),F_X(2))$ shows why convergence at a jump of the limiting CDF cannot be required?
If $X_n\xrightarrow{d}X$ and also $X_n\xrightarrow{d}Y$, what can be concluded?
options: Nothing; the two limits can have different laws

questions.question: Suppose $X_n\xrightarrow{d}X$, and $Y_n$ has the same distribution as $X_n$ for every $n$. What follows for $Y_n$?
options: $Y_n\xrightarrow{d}X$ only if the $Y_n$ are mutually independent
$Y_n\xrightarrow{d}X$ only if their means also converge

questions.question: Let $X_n$ be uniform on $(0,1+1/n)$, with $F_{X_n}(0.5)=0.5/(1+1/n)$. What is $\lim_{n\to\infty}F_{X_n}(0.5)$?
Real random variables $X_n$ and $X$ share a probability space and satisfy $\mathbb{P}(|X_n-X|>\varepsilon)\le1/(n\varepsilon)$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. Which conclusion follows?
options: $X_n\xrightarrow{d}X$ only if $X$ has a continuous CDF
$X_n\xrightarrow{d}X$ without any of these extra conditions

questions.question: Let $M_n$ be the maximum of $n$ independent uniform variables on $(0,1)$. For fixed $t>0$ and $n>t$, $\mathbb{P}(n(1-M_n)>t)=(1-t/n)^n$. What is the limit of this probability?
Let $X_n\sim\mathcal{N}(1/n,\,1+1/n)$, and let $\Phi$ be the standard normal CDF. What is $\lim_n\mathbb{P}(X_n\le2)$?
Let $X_n$ assign probability $1/n$ to each point in $\{1/n,2/n,\ldots,1\}$, so $X_n\xrightarrow{d}\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)$. What is $\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{P}(X_n=0.3)$?
Suppose $X_n\xrightarrow{d}X$ with $X\sim\operatorname{Exp}(1)$. What is $\lim_n\mathbb{P}(X_n>2)$?
Let $X\sim\operatorname{Bern}(\tfrac12)$ and $X_n\xrightarrow{d}X$. Must $\mathbb{P}(X_n\le1)\to1$?
options: Yes, because the CDFs must converge at every threshold
Yes, because convergence forces $X_n$ into the support of $X$
No, because the limiting CDF is discontinuous at this threshold
No, because distributional convergence controls only strict inequalities

questions.question: For positive integers $n$, let $X_n$ have density $f_n(x)=1+\cos(2\pi nx)$ on $(0,1)$ and zero elsewhere. On $(0,1)$ its CDF is $F_{X_n}(x)=x+\sin(2\pi nx)/(2\pi n)$. How do the laws of $X_n$ and their densities behave as $n$ grows?
options: The laws converge to $\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)$, although the densities fail to converge pointwise on $(0,1)$
The laws converge to $\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)$ because the densities converge pointwise to $1$
The laws fail to converge in distribution because the densities oscillate with $n$
The laws converge to the constant $\tfrac12$ because the densities are symmetric about $\tfrac12$

questions.question: Let $X_n=3-1/n$, and let $F$ be the CDF of the constant $3$. At which real $x$ does $F_{X_n}(x)\to F(x)$ fail?

Let $T_1,\ldots,T_n$ be independent lifetimes with CDF $F_T(t)=1-\mathrm{e}^{-t}$ for $t\ge0$ and $0$ otherwise. Put $M_n=\max(T_1,\ldots,T_n)$, and let $\log$ denote the natural logarithm. What is $\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{P}(M_n-\log n\le0)$?
Suppose $X_n\xrightarrow{d}X$, where $X$ has continuous CDF $F(x)=1/(1+\mathrm{e}^{-x})$ for real $x$. With $\log$ the natural logarithm, what is $\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{P}(-\log3<X_n\le\log3)$?

Let $Z$ and $W$ be independent $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ variables. Put $X_n=Z$ for all $n$, and $Y_n=Z$ for even $n$ but $Y_n=W$ for odd $n$. Both sequences have the standard normal law for every $n$. What happens to the laws of $S_n=X_n+Y_n$?
options: They converge to $\mathcal{N}(0,2)$ because the marginal variances add
They converge to $\mathcal{N}(0,4)$ because $S_n=2Z$ at even indices
They have no limit: even and odd indices give $\mathcal{N}(0,4)$ and $\mathcal{N}(0,2)$
They converge to $\mathcal{N}(0,3)$, the average of the two laws

questions.question: Suppose $X_n\xrightarrow{d}c$, where $c$ is a real constant and $F_{X_n}$ is the CDF of $X_n$. For fixed $\varepsilon>0$, which argument proves $\mathbb{P}(|X_n-c|>\varepsilon)\to0$?
options: Bound the error probability by $F_{X_n}(c-\varepsilon)+1-F_{X_n}(c+\varepsilon)$; both terms tend to $0$
Write the error probability as $1-F_{X_n}(c)$; CDF convergence at $c$ makes this tend to $0$
Write the error probability as $F_{X_n}(c+\varepsilon)-F_{X_n}(c-\varepsilon)$; this difference tends to $0$
Bound the error probability by $F_{X_n}(c-\varepsilon)$ alone; the lower-tail limit also controls the upper tail

questions.question: For integers $n\ge3$, let $X_n$ be geometric on $\{1,2,\ldots\}$ with success probability $2/n$, so $\mathbb{P}(X_n>k)=(1-2/n)^k$ for integers $k\ge0$. What is $\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{P}(X_n/n>3\mid X_n/n>1)$?
For integers $n\ge3$, let $X_n\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,2/n)$, with $\mathbb{P}(X_n=k)=\binom nk(2/n)^k(1-2/n)^{n-k}$ for $k=0,\ldots,n$. What is $\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{P}(X_n\le1)$?
